label: Rob’s simple title prompt
explanation: These original 18 examples let us try Rob’s simpler instructions: keep a clear title, clarify an unclear one, or separate descriptions that represent different kinds of work.
prompt:
﻿Title Clarification Parley Prompt
09/13/2026


Some colleagues and I are creating an ontology of work activities. It is structured as a knowledge graph, with general kinds of work activities, such as “Sell,” differentiated hierarchically from more specific kinds, such as “Sell Food” or “Sell Insurance.”


A key source for this ontology has been the US Dept of Labor's O*Net database. We extracted the core verb and direct object from each activity description in O*NET (including GWAs, IWAs, DWAs, and tasks) and used the resulting verb-direct object pairs as the titles of key nodes in our knowledge graph. We call these verb-direct object pairs “atomic activities,” and each was linked to the O*NET description(s) that served as their basis. 


When an O*NET description listed multiple core verbs, we created separate verb-direct object pairs to cover all the relevant verbs and direct objects. And when a verb-direct object pair was based on multiple O*NET descriptions, that verb-direct object was linked to all of the relevant O*NET descriptions from which it ws derived. 


In most cases, this approach worked well, but two issues arose:
* In some instances, the verb-direct object pair did not supply enough information for a non-expert user of the system to gain a clear, intuitive sense of underlying work activity. 
* In other instances, a verb-direct object pair was linked with more than one O*NET description, and they were different enough that we thought they should, rather than continuing to be grouped together, instead be grouped into separate categories, with each category given a new title. 


We’re now seeking to improve our ontology, and we'd like some help. The inputs will be: 
* verb-object pair, that is, the title of an atomic activity in our ontology
* list of all O*NET descriptions linked to that verb-direct object pair


For each verb-object pair, do the following;
* If a single O*NET description is linked to a verb-object pair, evaluate whether the current title conveys a clear, intuitively understandable sense of the work activity in question. If so, confirm that the current title is adequate. If not, propose a new title that is clearer and more readily understandable to a non-expert. When generating a new title, confine it to 2-5 words. In both cases, give a rationale. 
* If multiple O*NET descriptions are linked to a single verb-direct pair, evaluate whether all of these O*NET descriptions are similar enough that they warrant being grouped in a single category. If so, go on to evaluate the appropriateness of the title, as described in the step above. If not, group the O*NET descriptions into more appropriate categories and propose a new title for each, using the same approach described in the step above for creating new titles. If some of the O*NET descriptions in the list can still be appropriately linked to the original title, indicate that as well. In all cases, give a rationale.    
 


When considering how well a verb-direct object title captures the essence of a linked O*NET description, focus on the verb and direct object included in the title and ignore others. When an O*NET description includes compound verbs or compound direct objects, the additional verbs and direct objects will be covered by other atomic activities located in other areas in the ontology. 


Keep in mind these considerations when evaluating titles: 
* Semantic clarity: Does a title immediately convey what the activity is?
* Specificity vs. generality: Is there important context or scope that's missing?
* User intuitiveness: Would someone unfamiliar with O*NET understand what this activity involves?
* Consistency: Does it fit with the style/structure of other titles in the ontology?


When proposing new titles, please choose ones that are: 
* More descriptive (by adding additional context)
* More specific (by narrowing the scope when the verb-direct object is too broad)
* More colloquial (by using language that's more immediately understandable)


Outputs from the exercise should be:
* For titles with a single linked O*NET activity, indicate those for which
--the current title is adequate and should not be changed
--the current title is inadequate and should be changed, with proposed new title included 
* For titles linked to multiple O*NET descriptions, indicate those for which
--the existing grouping of O*NET descriptions and title are both adequate
--the existing grouping of O*NET descriptions is adequate but title is inadequate and should be changed, with proposed new title included
--the existing grouping of O*NET descriptions should be restructured, with proposed new groupings and proposed titles provided; also list all O*NET descriptions for which the existing title is still adequate
outputFormat: Output format for the software: return one JSON object with "groups" (a list of objects containing "title", "descriptionNumbers", and "reason") and "reason" (the overall rationale). "descriptionNumbers" contains the numbers of the O*NET descriptions supporting that group. These numbers identify descriptions in this input, not group numbers. Include the current title as a group if the current title is adequate for some or all descriptions. Keep rationales brief.
softwareChecks: Ordinary code checks whether the answer can be read, whether description numbers exist, and whether any description is missing or repeated. It flags empty groups, repeated titles, inconsistent grouping of identical descriptions, titles outside 2–5 words, and changes to the leading verb. A description supporting more than one group is shown as a representation-policy question. The code does not change the model answer, assign missing descriptions, decide semantic correctness, approve a grouping, or write to the ontology.

groups.title: Conduct Research
groups.reason: Retain the original title: these descriptions leave the research focus unspecified. Accompanying duties, publication settings, or sample examples do not establish a specialty.

groups.title: Research Waste and Pollution Management
groups.reason: Both investigate waste problems, treatment or disposal options, and methods of controlling environmental pollution.

groups.title: Conduct Agricultural Research
groups.reason: These share an agricultural focus, encompassing general farming research, animal production, and horticultural methods.

groups.title: Conduct Online and Library Research
groups.reason: Both specify research using online or library resources, making the information-source context useful in the title.

groups.title: Conduct Engineering Research
groups.reason: Adds the engineering context: investigating equipment and system feasibility, design, operation, or performance.

groups.title: Conduct Psychological Research
groups.reason: These investigate mental and behavioral functioning, psychological disorders, or diagnostic and therapeutic counseling methods.

groups.title: Research Crops for Biofuels
groups.reason: Both focus on plants as energy sources, including improving energy crops and investigating their use in fuel production.

groups.title: Conduct Work Systems Research
groups.reason: These study organizational behavior, work processes, and the equipment, staffing, or procedures that shape work systems.

groups.title: Conduct Robotics Research
groups.reason: Both investigate robotic technologies, mechanisms, systems, or capabilities.

groups.title: Conduct Nanotechnology Research
groups.reason: Identifies the distinctive focus on nanoscale materials, devices, processes, and applications.

groups.title: Conduct Cell and Gene Research
groups.reason: Both investigate cellular functions, gene regulation, and related molecular mechanisms.

groups.title: Conduct Biotechnology Research
groups.reason: Clarifies the applied biological focus spanning diagnostics, crop improvement, pharmaceuticals, and microbial waste recycling.

groups.title: Conduct Ecological Research
groups.reason: These examine natural or industrial ecosystems, industrial environmental impacts, and ecological sustainability.

groups.title: Conduct Environmental Economics Research
groups.reason: Both investigate connections between economic activity, environmental problems, and resource-use decisions.

groups.title: Research Allergies and Immune Function
groups.reason: Names the laboratory or clinical research subject in language more accessible than immunology alone.

groups.title: Conduct Medical Research
groups.reason: These describe general clinical or basic medical research, including anatomy, disease prevention, medications, and treatments.

groups.title: Conduct Eye Health Research
groups.reason: Makes the ophthalmology focus understandable without requiring familiarity with the specialty name.

groups.title: Conduct Sports Medicine Research
groups.reason: Both concern athletic training, sports medicine, or injuries and conditions associated with exercise.

groups.title: Conduct Market Research
groups.reason: These investigate markets, consumer opinions, buying behavior, product appeal, or marketing strategies.

groups.title: Research Nursing Information Systems
groups.reason: Clarifies nursing informatics as research concerning information and computing systems used in nursing.

groups.title: Research Light-Based Technologies
groups.reason: Expresses photonics research in more immediately understandable language.

groups.title: Research Mapping and Remote Sensing
groups.reason: These investigate related mapping methods, geographic software, and remote-sensing technologies.

groups.title: Research Women's and Infant Health
groups.reason: Captures the maternal, infant, contraceptive, breastfeeding, and gynecological research topics.

groups.title: Research Hearing, Speech, and Balance
groups.reason: The descriptions overlap in hearing research and extend to closely related speech and balance functions.

groups.title: Research Debt Relief Options
groups.reason: Clarifies that research seeks ways to prevent asset loss or address levies and wage garnishments.

groups.title: Conduct Music Therapy Research
groups.reason: Identifies research on music as a therapeutic practice, rather than music research generally.

groups.title: Conduct Economic Research
groups.reason: The economic subject is explicit, but no narrower economic specialty is specified.

groups.title: Conduct Weather and Climate Research
groups.reason: Both investigate atmospheric phenomena, covering weather processes and climate.

groups.title: Conduct Anthropological and Archaeological Research
groups.reason: Groups ethnographic fieldwork with related anthropological and archaeological investigation.

groups.title: Research Prospective Donors and Investors
groups.reason: These duplicate descriptions investigate prospective contributors' goals, wealth, giving history, and related donor-market information.

groups.title: Research User Needs for Design
groups.reason: Makes the design-requirements purpose explicit and distinguishes user research from general market research.

groups.title: Conduct Product Safety Research
groups.reason: Both investigate product or material safety, including fire safety and fire-retardant applications.

groups.title: Research Workplace Health Hazards
groups.reason: Translates industrial hygiene into its more intuitive focus on workplace exposures and health hazards.

groups.title: Research Instructional Content
groups.reason: Identifies the purpose of gathering subject knowledge to develop instructional materials.

groups.title: Conduct Background Research
groups.reason: These gather factual details or topic background to inform subsequent work, including survey preparation.

groups.title: Conduct Land Use Research
groups.reason: Names the shared subject of the economic, social, regulatory, and physical factors being investigated.

groups.title: Conduct Surgical Research
groups.reason: Both investigate improved surgical techniques; musculoskeletal surgery is a specialization within that activity.

groups.title: Conduct Radiation Therapy Research
groups.reason: Clarifies the focus on radiation cancer treatment and related planning systems or devices.

groups.title: Conduct Nutrition Research
groups.reason: These study diet and nutrition, including genetic influences and population-level health patterns.

groups.title: Conduct Social Research
groups.reason: These investigate social issues and societal patterns, including research advancing social work.

groups.title: Research Chemical Manufacturing Processes
groups.reason: Specifies the research goal of developing or improving chemical production processes.

groups.title: Conduct Occupational Therapy Research
groups.reason: Identifies the therapeutic field concerned with supporting participation in everyday activities.

groups.title: Conduct Historical Research
groups.reason: All investigate history; preservation applications and publication duties do not change that research focus.

groups.title: Research Specimen Restoration and Preservation
groups.reason: Distinguishes studying conservation methods from performing specimen restoration or preservation.

groups.title: Research Products and Processes
groups.reason: Preserves the stated research subjects without assuming an engineering, safety, or marketing purpose.

groups.title: Conduct Research for Creative Projects
groups.reason: Makes the purpose of informing art, design, or related creative work explicit.

groups.title: Conduct Mathematical Research
groups.reason: Specifies research aimed at advancing mathematical knowledge and theory.

groups.title: Conduct Biomedical Engineering Research
groups.reason: Identifies the engineering investigation of human and animal biological systems.

groups.title: Conduct Materials Science Research
groups.reason: Clarifies that research concerns physical materials' structures and properties for product development or improvement.

groups.title: Research Water Conservation
groups.reason: Names the water-resource protection and conservation focus without incorporating the separate communication activity.
